children: Hero Motors shares hit the 10 per cent lower circuit in Monday's trading session amid profit booking, days after the company's market debut.
Shares of the company were quoted at Rs 127.67 apiece on the BSE, down 10 per cent, the lowest permissible trading limit for the session.
Despite the fall, the stock was still up 55.7 per cent from its listing price of Rs 82 per share.

The stock opened at Rs 82 on the NSE, marking a 2.38 per cent discount to the IPO price of Rs 84 per share. On the BSE, Hero Motors shares debuted at Rs 82.10, translating into a 2.26 per cent discount to the issue price on September 23.
Hero Motors had fixed the IPO price band at Rs 79-84 per share. The Rs 1,000-crore issue comprised a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 600 crore and an offer-for-sale (OFS) component of Rs 400 crore.
Hero Motors said it plans to use Rs 190 crore from the fresh issue towards repayment or prepayment of certain borrowings.
Another Rs 200 crore has been earmarked for purchasing equipment for capacity expansion at its facility in Gautam Buddha Nagar, Uttar Pradesh.
The remaining proceeds will be used to fund inorganic growth through unidentified acquisitions and strategic initiatives, besides general corporate purposes.

title: Hero Motors shares hit 10% lower circuit; stock still up 56% from listing price
